question: What supported mechanism can deliver an authenticated coordination event to an intended existing local Codex Desktop chat and cause an observable turn while preserving identity, workspace and policy?

user_confirmed_scope.authority: User clarification relayed by parent researcher during this investigation
user_confirmed_scope.required: Resume an idle existing Codex Desktop chat while Desktop is running and workstation is awake
user_confirmed_scope.unavailable: Retain coordination messages while unavailable; launching Desktop or waking the workstation is not required
user_confirmed_scope.enforcement: Ownership enforced at admission and protected integration; private local investigation permitted

conclusion.summary: Current official queue/resume and App Server interfaces are candidates for a trusted local companion. They do not by themselves establish that this installed Desktop exposes its owning backend to that companion or consumes queued input in the intended idle local chat. No supported end-to-end automatic Desktop wake is established by this investigation.
conclusion.required_next_proof: For the actual installed Desktop build, demonstrate a documented, authorized route to its existing chat's owning backend, then authenticated event admission -> same chat UUID -> observable turn -> event-ID acknowledgement in Desktop, preserving workspace and policy. A separate headless/CLI session or cloud Work task fails this condition.

prototype_proposal.boundary: Small manually installed plugin plus per-user local companion; reusable authenticated event/recovery core with a Desktop-specific adapter only if supported attachment is established
steps: First gate: identify exact Desktop build, OS, backend owner and supported local attach/queue contract without token extraction or private IPC. Stop with a concrete upstream support gap if none is available.

Plugin SessionStart hook registers a main-chat binding through owner-only local IPC: opaque coordination identity, host/runtime instance, thread/session UUID relationship, workspace/project root, policy fingerprint, and generation. Never bind by title or arbitrary event-supplied UUID/path.

Companion authenticates service and recipient, validates access and binding generation, fetches permitted content, stores event ID/hash/expiry durably before attempting admission; treat event content as untrusted data.

Admission and protected integration enforce ownership. Queue ordinary busy-chat mail for a later turn; do not interrupt approval/question prompts. Only an expressly authorized steer uses the current expectedTurnId. Never synthesize Enter or answer prompts.

For an idle chat use the qualified owning-backend queue/resume or resume/start route. Do not create/fork or silently fall back to an embedded/headless server. Keep original model/workspace/sandbox/approval settings.

Persist event-to-queue/turn correlation and deduplication across companion restarts. If acknowledgement is uncertain, reconcile queue/history/event acknowledgement before resubmission. CLI creates new client IDs, so a zero exit or retry is not deduplication.

Keep unavailable events pending with backoff/expiry and explicit operator reconciliation. On Desktop restart renew generation and revalidate identity/workspace/policy before draining. Do not infer completed effects from read/delivered state.
required_receipts: Authenticated event received and durable event ID/hash stored
Target binding admitted: exact Desktop chat UUID, host/backend/build, workspace and policy fingerprint
Queued/submitted receipt with queue ID; record warnings separately
Observed new turn ID/status for exact same Desktop chat
Agent acknowledgement echoing synthetic event ID and expected workspace, visible in Desktop
Separate completed-action receipt if a task effect is requested
Negative cases: duplicate event, busy/permission-blocked chat, wrong identity/workspace/generation, unavailable host, restart with uncertain acknowledgement

unproven_capabilities: Installed Desktop offers a supported authorized third-party path to its actual owning local chat backend, across Windows/WSL boundary if used
That path can accept an event and start an observable turn in an already-idle existing Desktop chat without creating a different runtime/chat
Desktop and companion share defined writer, approval and notification ownership preserving policy and workspace
Version-specific queue support and reconnect/restart behavior on the owning backend
